title: Chapter 7 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of file reading, redirections, cut/sort/uniq, tr/sed, and grep!

questions.question: Which command shows the first 15 lines of a file?
questions.explanation: `head -n 15` or `head -15` displays the first 15 lines.

questions.question: What does `cat file1 file2 > combined` do?
options: Creates 'combined' containing the contents of file1 then file2
Merges file1 and file2 into file1
questions.explanation: `cat` concatenates, and `>` redirects output to a new file.

questions.question: How do you follow a growing log file in real time?
questions.explanation: `tail -f` follows the file, displaying new lines as they are written.

questions.question: Which `wc` option counts lines only?
questions.explanation: `-l` counts lines.

questions.question: What is the difference between `>` and `>>`?
questions.explanation: `>` truncates the file before writing; `>>` adds to the end.

questions.question: How can you redirect both stdout and stderr to `out.log` in one go?
questions.explanation: `> out.log 2>&1` and `&> out.log` are both valid Bash syntaxes.

questions.question: What does `tee -a file` do?
options: Reads from file and prints to stdout
Appends stdin to file and also prints to stdout
questions.explanation: `-a` makes tee append to the file instead of overwriting.

questions.question: Which `cut` delimiter sets a comma as the field separator?
questions.explanation: `-d,` specifies the delimiter (comma).

questions.question: What does `cut -c1-5 file` do?
options: Extracts characters 1 through 5 of each line
questions.explanation: `-c` operates on character positions.

questions.question: Which `sort` flag sorts numbers correctly (2 before 10)?
questions.explanation: `-n` enables numeric sort.

questions.question: Why is `sort file | uniq` used together?
options: `uniq` only removes duplicate lines that are next to each other
`uniq` requires sorted input to work at all
questions.explanation: `uniq` only detects adjacent duplicates, so sort first to group them.

questions.question: What does `tr 'a-z' 'A-Z' < input.txt` do?
questions.explanation: It translates lowercase to uppercase.

questions.question: Which `sed` command replaces the first 'cat' with 'dog' on each line?
questions.explanation: Both `s/cat/dog/` and `s|cat|dog|` work; the delimiter can be changed.

questions.question: What does the `g` flag in `sed 's/foo/bar/g'` do?
options: Replaces all occurrences on a line
questions.explanation: The `g` flag stands for global, substituting every match on the line.

questions.question: How can you delete the 5th line of a file with sed without modifying the original file?
questions.explanation: `sed '5d'` prints all lines except line 5; without `-i`, the original file stays untouched.

questions.question: What does `grep -v 'error' log` output?
questions.explanation: `-v` inverts the match, so it shows lines NOT matching the pattern.

questions.question: Which grep option searches recursively through directories?
questions.explanation: `-r` (or `-R`) recursively reads all files under each directory.

questions.question: To match whole words only with grep, use the ___ flag.
questions.explanation: `-w` ensures the pattern is surrounded by non‑word characters.

questions.question: What does the regular expression `^$` match?
questions.explanation: `^` is start of line, `$` is end of line; together they match a line with nothing between.

questions.question: How can you use grep in an if statement without printing anything?
questions.explanation: `-q` (quiet) suppresses output and returns an exit code, perfect for conditionals.
